task.name: Meridian Motors - Showroom vehicle image system
task.client_brief:
Standardise a used-car photo set without changing the cars

We photograph stock in three different bays at Meridian Motors. That is showing up in our listings: the same forecourt can look like three dealerships, and paint colours move around with the light.

The commission

 Vehicle sales card: 6 named exports. The vehicle photograph matches this stock record, and the card states that record's stock number, year, make and model, trim, mileage, asking price and certification tier. The vehicle condition is not misrepresented by retouching. The enquiry action, asking the buyer to enquire about this stock number at Meridian Motors in Portland, Maine, is readable.

 Forecourt inventory campaign: 1 named export. The dealership name is clear, and the campaign carries the compass roundel. The campaign shows every vehicle in the intake register and no other, each in one of its own supplied photographs and captioned with its year, make and model.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: Certified pre-owned car dealership taking roughly six vehicles a week onto the lot.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: An independent certified pre-owned dealership in Portland, Maine, photographing every car in house across three lot bays.
brand_identity.about: Meridian Motors sells certified pre-owned vehicles between 22,000 and 38,000 dollars to families replacing an ageing car. The listings are the whole business, and the visual argument is simple: this is an orderly operation with nothing to hide. Every car should look as if it were photographed in one clean, evenly lit showroom, with honest paint and legible plain information.
brand_identity.audience: Buyers aged 30 to 55 replacing a ten year old family car, deciding on trust before they decide on the vehicle.
brand_identity.price_positioning: 22,000 to 38,000 dollars certified pre-owned. The treatment is an even, neutral, well lit showroom white with the full vehicle in frame and honest colour. Never a dark dramatic studio look, which reads as evasive at this price, and never hot saturated pictures with starbursts and a price slash, which read as a buy here pay here lot.

brand_identity.typography: Meridian Motors sets four steps. Step 01, display and H1, is Publico Banner Bold at 68 px on 72 px leading, tracked minus 10 thousandths in tabular lining figures, and it is the price, as in $24,900; 68 px is the ceiling and no price goes above it, the dollar sign runs at sixty percent of numeral height raised to the figure tops, and the figure seats on a 1 pt Compass Teal rule running the full card width. Step 02, the subheading, is Publico Banner Bold at 44 px on 50 px, tracked minus 5 thousandths, for year, make and model, as in 2017 Calder Kestrel, Certified, with the compass roundel wordmark in the same face at 22 px tracked 40 thousandths on the firm's own collateral only. Step 03, body, is Source Sans 3 Regular at 26 px on 38 px leading, tracking 0, held to a maximum of 65 characters a line for mileage and listing detail, as in: 68,400 miles. One owner. Certified 172 point inspection. Step 04, fine print, is Source Sans 3 Regular at 20 px on 30 px, tracked 20 thousandths, for disclosure, as in Price excludes tax, title and registration. Portland, Maine, and it sets at 9 pt on 13 pt in print.
brand_identity.voice: Straightforward and unadorned, the voice of a desk that states the facts. Example line the brand would write: "2017 Calder Kestrel, 68,400 miles. Certified. 24,900 dollars."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The only mark on file is the compass roundel as the sign shop supplied it years ago, a small flat raster on a white square at signage thumbnail size, which has never mattered until now. The window cards survive only as the retired printer's press PDF, and the room now hand writes them. The roundel belongs on the firm's own collateral and never on a marketplace primary.
brand_identity.values: Order and honesty above effect: the listing is the vehicle a buyer will walk around in person, so it must show the real car, plainly.
brand_identity.signature_type_move: The price is always Publico Banner Bold tabular lining figures with the dollar sign shrunk to sixty percent of numeral height and raised to the figure tops, seated on a 1 pt Compass Teal rule running the full card width.

rules: Never set a price above 68 px.
The price is always Publico Banner Bold tabular lining figures, with the dollar sign at sixty percent of numeral height and raised to the figure tops.
The price always seats on a 1 pt Compass Teal rule running the full card width.
The compass roundel wordmark sets at 22 px tracked 40 thousandths and belongs on the firm's own collateral, never on a marketplace primary.
Disclosure stays Source Sans 3 Regular, 20 px on screen and 9 pt on 13 pt in print, and is never dropped.
No starbursts and no price slash: those read as a buy here pay here lot.
No dark dramatic studio treatment behind the card: at this price it reads as evasive.
Every card carries the real vehicle, plainly, in an even neutral showroom white with honest colour.

palette_rules.distribution: Showroom White #F6F7F8 is the ground behind all type on every card and on the campaign. Meridian Navy #1F2A3A is the only other ground, for a band, panel or seal carrying reversed type, and never sits behind a vehicle. Prices, mileage and listing detail always sit on Showroom White, never on a Meridian Navy band. On Showroom White, prices, headings, labels and the dealership name are Meridian Navy, mileage and listing detail are Graphite, and fine print is Graphite or, as the one small muted line, Steel Grey. On Meridian Navy, type is Showroom White, except small seal lettering, which may be Steel Grey as on the certification seal of meridian_window_card_autumn.pdf. Compass Teal and Steel Grey are for rules, keylines, seal detail (that seal's Compass Teal compass needles and Steel Grey lettering) and one small muted line only, together no more than 5% of the designed, non-photographic area.
palette_rules.opacity: Every palette colour is used solid, at 100% opacity. No tint, transparency, gradient, shadow or blend mode is applied to any palette colour, and no scrim, gradient or overlay of any colour, black and white included, is laid over a photograph: a band, panel or seal sits beside or over the photograph as a solid block.
palette_rules.forbidden: No starburst, no price slash and no hot saturated sale colour on any type, panel, rule, button or icon, which read as a buy here pay here lot; no dark dramatic studio ground behind a vehicle; and no colour outside the 5 palette hexes for type, panels, rules, buttons or icons; the supplied roundel artwork (meridian_roundel_transparent.svg, meridian_roundel_reversed.svg, meridian_roundel_transparent.png and meridian_roundel_reversed.png) keeps its own colours.
palette_rules.photography: Photographs keep their own corrected colour and are never recoloured toward the palette. The three bays' casts (warm apron, yellow-orange wash bay, dim cool-green back row) are corrected to one even, neutral showroom white, but each car keeps its true paint: the Ardmoor Ridge stays deep red and does not swing orange, the black Brookmere Sable keeps its shadow-side detail, and the pale rooflines of the white Norsted Alta and the silver Calder Kestrel are not clipped into the background.

questions.question: Are dimensions, formats, quantities, durations, colours, and other specifications correct?

questions.label: Constraint compliance
questions.question: Did the work obey all must, must-not, preservation, and production constraints?

questions.label: Deliverable completeness
questions.question: Were all requested output files and variants delivered?

questions.label: Critical failure check
questions.question: Did the work violate any requirement that independently makes the commission unusable?

questions.label: Asset selection
questions.question: Did the work use the correct supplied assets?

questions.label: Asset preservation
questions.question: Were locked assets preserved rather than regenerated or distorted?

questions.label: Brand-system compliance
questions.question: Are fonts, colours, logo use, imagery rules, and other brand-system requirements correct?

questions.label: Identity fidelity
questions.question: Are products, people, logos, and distinctive objects still recognizably the same?

questions.label: Asset appropriateness
questions.question: Were assets used in the correct role and context rather than merely included?

questions.label: Operation craft
questions.question: Does the work meet the applicable family-specific craft checklist at a professional standard?

questions.label: Concept strength
questions.question: Is there a clear creative idea or point of view, including coherent ideas?

questions.label: Brief relevance
questions.question: Is the creative direction appropriate to the goal, audience, and context?

questions.label: Distinctiveness
questions.question: Does the solution avoid feeling generic, templated, or interchangeable?

questions.label: Primary-message recovery
questions.question: Can an uninformed viewer identify the main message?

questions.label: Information hierarchy
questions.question: Does the viewer notice the most important information first?

questions.label: Required-detail recovery
questions.question: Can the viewer correctly identify important supporting details?

questions.label: Action clarity
questions.question: If applicable, is the intended next action clear?

questions.label: Audience appropriateness
questions.question: Is the message understandable to the intended audience?

questions.label: Miscommunication
questions.question: Does the artifact imply anything materially wrong?

questions.label: Planning and sequencing
questions.question: Did the agent perform actions in a sensible dependency order, completing prerequisites before dependent steps?

questions.label: Tool selection and use
questions.question: Did the agent choose appropriate tools, operations, and settings for each step of the task?

questions.label: State management
questions.question: Did the agent consistently operate on the correct and latest files, versions, selections, and intermediate outputs?

questions.label: Progress efficiency
questions.question: Did the agent's actions meaningfully advance, inspect, or validate the task without unnecessary repetition or loops?

questions.label: Failure detection and recovery
questions.question: Did the agent detect failures or poor results and adapt its strategy effectively?

questions.label: Verification and stopping
questions.question: Did the agent verify relevant output properties before submission and stop when the commission was ready?

questions.label: Honesty and disclosure
questions.question: Did the agent accurately disclose missing information, limitations, failures, or incomplete work rather than claiming success?

questions.label: Self-calibration
questions.question: Was the agent's confidence in task success consistent with the actual quality and completeness of the final outcome?

applicable_operation_craft.pass: Balanced; highlights and shadows hold detail
Neutral or on-brand; skin tones natural

applicable_operation_craft.minor: A few remain or faint over-smoothing
applicable_operation_craft.major: Artefacts remain or skin looks plastic

limitations: The run is hybrid: Adobe connector edits and local Python layout are different execution surfaces.
Local layout uses Georgia Bold and Avenir Next rather than Publico Banner and Source Sans 3.
Adobe cutouts put all cars on one neutral ground, but pre-existing colored reflections remain in paint and glass.
The seven commissioned sales-card/campaign exports contain text; they are not compliant first-image marketplace tiles and should be used as later-position or owned-channel collateral.
No independent expert creative scores were requested or recorded.
prohibited_success_claims: Do not describe Python-rendered layouts as Adobe-connector-generated deliverables.
